hypothesis: A symmetric fixed take-profit may reduce peak-profit giveback without destroying the exact aligned-entry v52 HYPE route's after-cost edge.
recommendation: Do not add a symmetric fixed take-profit to the live v52 HYPE route.
why_now: The operator questioned whether profitable HYPE lifecycles were remaining open long enough to give back gains. The exact v52 aligned-entry development cohort now supports a fixed-entry target comparison without changing entry selection.
evidence_reviewed: The exact aligned-only v52 HYPE development cohort: 41 completed lifecycles, 19 long and 22 short.
The previously opened later-confirmation cohort: one completed aligned long lifecycle.
A predeclared 40/60/80/100/150/200/300/500-bps target grid with 4.5-bps fees per side, hourly funding, 2-bps nominal target-exit slippage, and a 5-bps target-exit tail sensitivity.
The native opposite-signal, protective-stop, 8-hour regime review, and 24-hour hard-fallback control on identical entries.
observed_problem_or_opportunity: A fixed target could reduce giveback and largest-winner dependence, but it also truncates the large long trends on which the aligned HYPE cohort currently depends.
applicable_market_regime: Both-side HYPE compression-breakout entries with structural and breakout-side agreement under the exact v52 execution contract.
alternatives_considered: Retain the native opposite-signal, 80-bps protective stop, regime-supported soft hold, and 24-hour hard fallback.
Use the previously rejected 25/40/60-bps activation trailing locks.
Use the deferred 100-bps activation and 25-bps mature profit floor.
Add one symmetric fixed target from 40 through 500 bps.
Investigate a side-specific short target only after independent short-side evidence; do not select it post hoc from this development cohort.
expected_upside: No supported live upside. The development-selected 500-bps target improved leave-largest net by 252.285453 bps and the short slice by 918.699008 bps under target-exit tail slippage, but reduced total net by 1269.499749 bps and changed the long slice from +2098.274027 bps to -89.924729 bps.
main_risks_and_failure_modes: Every 40-300-bps target lost money after costs in development.
The 500-bps target remained positive but captured less than half the native aggregate net return.
The apparent 500-bps short-side improvement is a post-hoc directional slice with no later short confirmation.
The single later-confirmation long never reached 500 bps MFE, so it provides no independent target execution evidence.
One-minute OHLC cannot prove intrabar target-versus-stop ordering or private IOC execution; the native exit was conservatively given precedence on its own exit bar.
Fixed-entry sensitivity does not model additional signals that an earlier target exit could free capital to take.
validation_still_required: Capture the first exact v52 HYPE live lifecycle with entry, exit reason, opposite-signal state, stop behavior, fees, funding, slippage, MFE, MAE, and peak giveback.
Collect independent resolved long and short lifecycles before reopening any side-specific target hypothesis.
Require a predeclared side-specific experiment to remain positive after costs, across folds, and without its largest winner before requesting a live change.
success_metrics: A future predeclared challenger exceeds native total after-cost net return and leave-largest net return on unchanged entries.
The improvement is not created by converting the opposite direction from strongly positive to negative.
Independent live or later-window target triggers reconcile to executable fills and measured slippage.
failure_or_rollback_triggers: Any live fixed target would be rejected or rolled back if aggregate net, either configured side, or measured target execution deteriorated versus its frozen native control.
This rejected hypothesis may be reopened only with new independent side-specific evidence, a materially changed regime, or a changed execution assumption.
confidence_level: high on fixed-entry arithmetic and rejection of this symmetric grid; medium on broader exit optimality because the cohort has 41 development trades, one later-confirmation long, and no independent short confirmation
highest_value_next_investigation: Audit the first eligible v52 HYPE lifecycle end to end; do not retune the exit again before independent live evidence arrives.

superseded_reports.reason: The first report mislabeled every target trigger as zero because the summary expected a different status literal. Economics were unchanged, but trigger telemetry was invalid.
The second report fixed trigger counts but retained a breadth-first development selector that allowed a losing target to outrank the only profitable candidate.

limitations: The fixed-entry study cannot model additional signals that an earlier target exit could free capital to take.
One-minute OHLC cannot prove intrabar target-versus-stop ordering or private IOC execution.
The later-confirmation cohort contains one long and no short, so it cannot validate a side-specific short target.
The selected 500-bps target was selected on development only and reduced total after-cost net return versus the native exit.
falsifier: A predeclared independent both-side or explicitly side-specific fixed-target experiment, with source-compatible entries and executable costs, beats the native exit in total and leave-largest net return without materially degrading the opposite direction.
